title: Past Simple vs used to
grammarNote:
Past Simple и "used to" оба описывают прошлое, но означают РАЗНЫЕ вещи:

📌 PAST SIMPLE — конкретное событие в конкретный момент:
   "I visited my grandmother last week." (один конкретный раз)
   "She called me at 9 pm yesterday." (конкретный момент)

📌 USED TO — повторяющаяся привычка / состояние, которое изменилось:
   "I used to visit my grandmother every Sunday." (регулярно, но уже нет)
   "She used to call me every evening." (привычка в прошлом)

🔑 Тест: можно добавить "every day / regularly"?
✅ Да → used to: "I used to exercise every morning."
❌ Нет (один раз) → Past Simple: "I exercised yesterday morning."

grammarTable.subject: Past Simple — specific event
grammarTable.example: We went to the Nauryz festival last year.

grammarTable.subject: Past Simple — completed action
grammarTable.example: She prepared Nauryz kozhe on March 21st.

grammarTable.subject: used to — repeated habit
grammarTable.example: We used to go to the big city festival every year.

grammarTable.subject: used to — past state
grammarTable.example: They used to have a yurt in their garden.

grammarTable.subject: BOTH can be used
grammarTable.example: I walked to school. / I used to walk to school.

grammarTable.subject: Past Simple — NOT "used to"
grammarTable.example: She visited Almaty in 2020. (NOT: she used to visit in 2020)

grammarTable.subject: "used to" — NOT Past Simple
grammarTable.example: He used to smoke. (can't say: he smoked = unclear if habit)

grammarTable.subject: Time words help decide
grammarTable.short: when I was young = used to
grammarTable.example: She visited in 2018. / She used to visit when she was young.

grammarExtra.title: When to use Past Simple (NOT "used to")

rows.form: A single event at a specific time
rows.example: She visited Nauryz celebrations in Uralsk in 2021.

rows.form: A sequence of events (then... then... then...)
rows.example: She arrived, put on her dress, and walked to the celebration.

rows.form: A completed state for a specific period
rows.example: He was in Almaty for two weeks in 2023.

rows.form: An interrupting event in a narrative
rows.example: While we were cooking, grandmother arrived.

rows.form: With specific time references: yesterday, on Monday, in 1969
rows.example: Pushkin visited Uralsk in 1833. (specific date → Past Simple)

rows.form: Situations that occurred only once
rows.example: She made Nauryz kozhe for the first time last year.

grammarExtra.title: When to use "used to" (NOT Past Simple alone)

rows.form: A repeated past habit (implies: not anymore)
rows.example: We used to have big Nauryz parties. (we don't now)

rows.form: A long-lasting past state (implies: changed now)
rows.example: She used to be very shy. (she isn't now)

rows.form: Contrasting past vs present
rows.example: People used to travel by horse — now everyone drives.

rows.form: With when I was young / as a child / in those days / back then
rows.example: When I was young, we used to make Nauryz kozhe outdoors.

rows.form: Something that was true for a long time (not a specific day)
rows.example: He used to play the dombra. (over many years)

rows.form: NOT for single events — it implies repeated pattern
rows.example: She used to arrive late. (= she was always late, not once)

rows.form: Past Simple: "She walked to school."
rows.example: Could mean once, or could be a habit — context unclear.

rows.form: "used to": "She used to walk to school."
rows.example: Clear: this was a regular habit, and she no longer does it.

rows.form: Past Simple in a story/narrative
rows.example: She woke up, got dressed, and walked to school.

rows.form: "used to" for background habit in a story
rows.example: She used to walk to school, but one day she took the bus.

rows.form: "would" for past habits (same as "used to")
rows.example: She would walk to school every day. (literary/formal)

rows.form: "would" CANNOT replace "used to" for states
rows.example: She used to be poor. ✓ / She would be poor. ✗ (incorrect)

rows.form: Past Simple for something that happened once at Nauryz
rows.example: Last year, she made Nauryz kozhe for the first time. (= once, Past Simple)

rows.form: "used to" impossible with a specific time
rows.example: She used to visit Almaty in 2021. ✗ (2021 is a specific year — use Past Simple)

rows.form: "How long" questions → Past Simple
rows.example: How long did she live there? (specific duration → Past Simple, not used to)

rows.form: "used to" with stative verbs (know, believe, think, have)
rows.example: He used to know the recipe. / We used to have a yurt. ✓

rows.form: Negative of Past Simple ≠ negative of "used to"
rows.example: She didn't celebrate Nauryz last year. vs She didn't use to celebrate Nauryz (ever).

rows.form: Do not confuse "be used to" (accustomed) with "used to"
rows.example: I am used to spicy food. (= accustomed) ≠ I used to eat spicy food. (past habit)

grammarTip:
Быстрый тест:
"Это было регулярно / снова и снова?" → used to ✅
"Это было один раз / в конкретный момент?" → Past Simple ✅

"I _____ smoke." (курил — прошлая привычка) → USED TO smoke
"I _____ a cigarette yesterday." (один раз) → smoked
"She _____ live in Paris." (раньше жила, сейчас нет) → USED TO live
"She _____ to Paris last year." (поехала один раз) → went

exercises.text: She ___ Nauryz kozhe for the first time last week.
exercises.hint: "For the first time last week" = a single completed event → Past Simple.

exercises.text: When Amir was young, his family ___ set up a big yurt for Nauryz every year.
exercises.hint: "Every year when young" = repeated past habit → "used to".

exercises.text: Kamila ___ the museum in Uralsk with her class last Thursday.
People ___ travel by horse before cars were invented.
exercises.hint: Before cars = long past habit that no longer exists → "used to".

opts: He used to know the answer.
She used to arrive in Uralsk in 2019.
They used to have a big family.
exercises.correct: She used to arrive in Uralsk in 2019.
exercises.hint: "In 2019" is a specific time → must use Past Simple: "She arrived in Uralsk in 2019."

exercises.instruction: Complete with Past Simple or "used to".
exercises.text: When she was a child, Kamila ___ (not/like) traditional music. Now she loves it.
exercises.hint: "When she was a child... now she loves it" = past state vs present contrast → "used to".

exercises.text: Last Nauryz, they ___ fifty guests at their home.
exercises.hint: "Last Nauryz" = specific past event → Past Simple.

exercises.text: My grandfather ___ the dombra every evening as a child.
exercises.hint: Regular childhood habit (every evening) that no longer continues → "used to".

exercises.text: "She walked to school." vs "She used to walk to school." — what is the key difference?
opts: Past Simple is single/unclear; "used to" clearly shows a repeated habit
Past Simple is about the future
exercises.correct: Past Simple is single/unclear; "used to" clearly shows a repeated habit
exercises.hint: "used to walk" is unambiguous: it was a regular habit that has now stopped.

exercises.text: He ___ (not/be) interested in history. Then he visited the museum and changed his mind.
exercises.hint: Past state that changed: "didn't use to be" (negative of "used to" for states).

exercises.text: She arrived home, changed clothes, and ___ the Nauryz song with her family.
exercises.hint: Sequence of events in a narrative → Past Simple (arrived... changed... sang).

exercises.instruction: Identify which sentence is about a past STATE.
exercises.text: Choose the sentence describing a past state with "used to".
opts: She used to walk to school.
He used to visit his grandmother.
They used to run to school.
I used to be afraid of speaking English.
exercises.correct: I used to be afraid of speaking English.
exercises.hint: "Be afraid" is a state (not an action) → "used to be" describes a past state.

questions.text: Which sentence uses the correct form?
When Kamila was young, she ___ dance at every Nauryz celebration.
He ___ (visit) the museum last year for the first time.
questions.hint: "Last year, for the first time" = single specific event → Past Simple.

opts: A repeated past habit or long state that has ended
questions.correct: A repeated past habit or long state that has ended
questions.hint: "used to" = something that was regular or true in the past but is no longer.

questions.text: "She used to arrive in Uralsk in 2020" is correct.
questions.hint: "In 2020" is a specific year — use Past Simple: "She arrived in Uralsk in 2020."

questions.text: She arrived, greeted everyone, and ___ at the table.
questions.hint: Sequence of events in a narrative → Past Simple.

questions.text: People ___ travel by horse in Central Asia before modern transport.
questions.hint: Long past habit (before modern transport) that no longer exists → "used to".

questions.text: She ___ (not/like) spicy food when she was a child. Now she loves it.
questions.hint: Past habit/state that changed = negative "used to": didn't use to like.

questions.text: "would" can replace "used to" for past STATES (like "used to be").
questions.hint: "would" can only replace "used to" for HABITS: "I would go" ✓. But NOT for states: "I would be poor" ✗.

questions.text: Time expression test: which goes with "used to"?
questions.hint: "When I was a child/young/in those days" goes with "used to".

questions.text: "I am used to spicy food" and "I used to eat spicy food" mean the same thing.
questions.hint: "be used to" = be accustomed to (present). "used to eat" = past habit (no longer true).

questions.text: He ___ (know) the answer in those days, but he has forgotten now.
questions.hint: "In those days... but now forgotten" = past state that has changed → "used to know".

questions.text: Last spring, Kamila ___ (attend) a big Nauryz concert in the city centre.
questions.hint: "Last spring" = specific past event → Past Simple.

questions.text: Which sentence clearly shows a PAST HABIT (not ambiguous)?
opts: She used to walk to school.
questions.correct: She used to walk to school.
questions.hint: "used to walk" unambiguously shows a repeated past habit that has now stopped.

questions.text: Kamila ___ (not/be) confident in English. Now she speaks fluently.
questions.hint: Past state contrasted with present: negative "used to": didn't use to be.

questions.text: She ___ the dombra at the Nauryz concert last Saturday. Everyone loved it.
questions.hint: "Last Saturday at the concert" = specific single event → Past Simple.
